name: JM Press
description: The JM press is a powerlifting-derived tricep exercise invented by JM Blakley that blends a close-grip bench press and a skull crusher. The bar is unracked and lowered to the neck area with the elbows moving forward (past the bar's path), then pressed back to lockout. The position combines elbow flexion and shoulder flexion, loading the triceps in a unique way that transfers directly to lockout strength in the bench press. It is primarily used by powerlifters for tricep mass and strength.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a flat bench, bar in a close-grip bench press position (hands slightly inside shoulder width). Bar pressed to full extension.
execution.setup_instructions: Have a spotter. Use a moderate load — lighter than your close-grip bench press. This is a technical movement requiring practice.
steps: Step 1: Lower the bar toward the neck, allowing the elbows to push forward and down simultaneously.
Step 2: The bar travels toward the throat or chin as the elbows drop below the bar path.
Step 3: The bar barely touches or floats just above the throat.
Step 4: Drive the bar back to the starting position by extending the elbows and pushing the arms back.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on press.
common_mistakes: Attempting heavy loads before mastering the technique
Letting the bar rest on the throat rather than controlling it
safety_considerations: This exercise involves the bar approaching the throat — always use a spotter
Master lighter loads before increasing weight
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Bar to throat level at the bottom, full lockout at the top.
coaching_cues: Think skull crusher + close-grip press hybrid
